answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. A rotating committee samples claims and checks them against signed task receipts; one ember of suspicion is not enough, but repeated mismatches trigger review. The kernel is that creating a thousand names does not create a thousand trustworthy votes: each name ties up real capital and risks forfeiture. An attacker must therefore fund every sybil and keep the stake exposed for as long as the pulse of audits continues.
